name: Ajanta Caves
blurb: 30 rock-cut Buddhist caves in a horseshoe gorge, carved between the 2nd century BCE and 6th century CE, famous for painted murals of the Jataka tales.

name: Ellora Caves
blurb: 34 caves cut side by side — Buddhist, Hindu and Jain — crowned by the Kailasa Temple, carved top-down from a single basalt cliff.

name: Agra Fort
blurb: Mughal red-sandstone fortress on the Yamuna, built by Akbar and later the site of Shah Jahan's confinement, with a clear view of the Taj.

name: Taj Mahal
blurb: Shah Jahan's white-marble mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal, finished in 1653 and inlaid with semi-precious stone — best seen at sunrise, before the crowds.

name: Sun Temple, Konark
blurb: A 13th-century temple built as a colossal stone chariot for the sun god, its wheels carved as working sundials, half-ruined but still monumental.

name: Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram
blurb: Pallava-era rock-cut shrines and the Shore Temple facing the Bay of Bengal, alongside the giant open-air relief known as Arjuna's Penance.

name: Kaziranga National Park
blurb: Assam grassland and swampland reserve holding the world's largest population of one-horned rhinoceros, best explored by jeep or elephant-back safari.

name: Manas Wildlife Sanctuary
blurb: Foothill forest on the Bhutan border sheltering tigers, elephants and the rare golden langur — quieter and far less visited than Kaziranga.

name: Keoladeo National Park
blurb: A former royal duck-hunting marsh near Bharatpur, now a wetland sanctuary drawing thousands of migratory birds every winter.

name: Churches and Convents of Goa
blurb: 16th–17th century Portuguese churches in Old Goa, including the Basilica of Bom Jesus, which holds the relics of St. Francis Xavier.
_note: Serial property; coordinates for Old Goa cluster.

name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
blurb: Chandela-dynasty temples from the 10th–11th centuries, celebrated for intricately carved sculpture — only a fraction of the original 85 temples survive.

name: Group of Monuments at Hampi
blurb: The boulder-strewn ruins of Vijayanagara's capital — temples, bazaars and a stone chariot spread across a landscape that looks otherworldly at dawn.

name: Fatehpur Sikri
blurb: Akbar's short-lived red-sandstone capital, abandoned within 15 years for lack of water — its palaces and the towering Buland Darwaza remain intact.

name: Group of Monuments at Pattadakal
blurb: A cluster of 7th–8th century Chalukya temples blending northern and southern Indian temple styles side by side on the Malaprabha river.

name: Elephanta Caves
blurb: A short ferry ride from Mumbai's Gateway of India to rock-cut Shiva shrines, centred on a monumental three-faced Sadashiva sculpture.

nearestAirport.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai (BOM)

name: Great Living Chola Temples
blurb: Three living Shiva temples built over three centuries by Chola kings, headlined by the towering 11th-century Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur.
_note: Serial property (Thanjavur, Gangaikondacholapuram, Darasuram); coords for Thanjavur.

name: Sundarbans National Park
blurb: The world's largest mangrove forest, shared with Bangladesh, explored by boat through tidal channels where the Bengal tiger still swims between islands.

name: Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks
blurb: A high-Himalayan wilderness of alpine meadows and snow peaks around Nanda Devi, open to trekkers only through the short monsoon bloom.

name: Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi
blurb: India's best-preserved Buddhist stupa complex, founded by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, with elaborately carved gateways added later by the Sungas.

name: Humayun's Tomb
blurb: A garden tomb built for the Mughal emperor Humayun in the 1560s, and the direct architectural template for the Taj Mahal decades later.

name: Qutb Minar and its Monuments
blurb: A 73-metre tapering minaret begun in 1193 to mark the start of Delhi's Sultanate era, standing beside an even older iron pillar.

name: Mountain Railways of India
blurb: Three narrow-gauge Himalayan lines — Darjeeling, Nilgiri and Kalka–Shimla — still climbing steep grades on steam and diesel toy trains.
_note: Serial property (Darjeeling, Nilgiri, Kalka-Shimla); coords for Darjeeling Himalayan Railway.

name: Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya
blurb: The site where the Buddha is believed to have attained enlightenment, under a descendant of the original Bodhi tree — still an active pilgrimage site.

name: Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka
blurb: Sandstone rock shelters with paintings spanning the Mesolithic to medieval periods — among the earliest evidence of human life in India.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (formerly Victoria Terminus)
blurb: A Victorian Gothic railway station in daily use, its spires and turrets modelled on London's St Pancras and still Mumbai's busiest terminus.

nearestAirport.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai (BOM)

name: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park
blurb: An abandoned 16th-century sultanate capital at the foot of Pavagadh hill, blending Hindu and Islamic architecture across mosques, tombs and stepwells.

name: Red Fort
blurb: Shah Jahan's red-sandstone citadel and seat of Mughal power for two centuries — every Independence Day, the Prime Minister addresses the nation from its ramparts.

name: The Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
blurb: An 18th-century open-air observatory of stone astronomical instruments built by Maharaja Jai Singh II, including the world's largest stone sundial.

name: Western Ghats
blurb: A mountain range older than the Himalayas, running down India's west coast — one of the world's biodiversity hotspots across 39 protected pockets.
_note: Serial property, 39 components across 4 states; approximate central point.

name: Hill Forts of Rajasthan
blurb: Six hilltop Rajput forts, including Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh, built between the 5th and 18th centuries to guard the kingdoms below.
_note: Serial property (Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber, Jaisalmer); coords for Chittorgarh Fort.

name: Rani-ki-Vav (the Queen's Stepwell) at Patan, Gujarat
blurb: An 11th-century stepwell built as a memorial by a Solanki queen, its seven descending levels carved with over 500 sculptures.

nearestAirport.name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport, Ahmedabad (AMD)

name: Great Himalayan National Park Conservation Area
blurb: A steep Himachal wilderness of conifer forest and alpine pasture, home to snow leopards and blue sheep, reached mainly on foot.

name: Archaeological Site of Nalanda Mahavihara at Nalanda, Bihar
blurb: Ruins of the ancient world's largest residential university, teaching Buddhist philosophy to students from across Asia from the 5th to 12th centuries.

nearestAirport.name: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna (PAT)

name: Khangchendzonga National Park
blurb: A Sikkim reserve wrapped around the world's third-highest peak, sacred to local communities and home to red pandas and snow leopards.

name: The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier
blurb: The Capitol Complex — Chandigarh's Secretariat, Assembly and High Court — designed by Le Corbusier as the centrepiece of India's first planned city.
_note: Transnational serial property (17 sites/7 countries); India's component is the Complexe du Capitole, Chandigarh.

name: Historic City of Ahmadabad
blurb: A 15th-century walled city of carved-wood havelis and stepped pols, founded by Sultan Ahmad Shah on the banks of the Sabarmati.

name: Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai
blurb: Two adjoining South Mumbai precincts — Gothic Revival civic buildings around Oval Maidan facing an Art Deco skyline along Marine Drive.
_note: Two adjoining South Mumbai precincts; coords for Oval Maidan precinct.

name: Jaipur City, Rajasthan
blurb: Rajasthan's pink-washed walled capital, planned in 1727 on a precise grid of nine blocks around the City Palace and Hawa Mahal.

name: Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple, Telangana
blurb: A 13th-century Kakatiya temple with a roof said to be light enough to float on water, and sandstone carving famed for its detail.

name: Dholavira: a Harappan City
blurb: A 5,000-year-old Indus Valley city in the Rann of Kutch, with stone reservoirs and a stadium-sized ceremonial ground still visible today.

name: Santiniketan
blurb: The university town Rabindranath Tagore built around open-air classrooms and rural craft, still run on the Visva-Bharati philosophy he founded in 1921.

name: Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas
blurb: Star-shaped 12th–13th century temples at Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura, carved by Hoysala sculptors in soapstone fine enough to resemble ivory.
_note: Serial property (Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura); coords for Chennakeshava Temple, Belur.

name: Moidams – the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty
blurb: Earthen burial mounds of the Ahom dynasty at Charaideo, raised over six centuries and sometimes called Assam's own pyramids.

name: Maratha Military Landscapes of India
blurb: Twelve hill, forest and coastal forts built by the Maratha empire, headlined by Shivaji's mountain stronghold at Raigad.

nearestAirport.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai (BOM)

_note: Serial property (12 forts, Maharashtra & Tamil Nadu); coords for Raigad Fort.

name: Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath
blurb: The deer park where the Buddha gave his first sermon after enlightenment, marked today by the Ashoka pillar and the great Dhamek Stupa.

nearestAirport.name: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi (VNS)

name: Somnath Temple
blurb: The first of the twelve Jyotirlingas, on Gujarat's Arabian Sea coast — rebuilt several times after historic raids, its current shikhara dates to 1951.

name: Mallikarjuna Temple
blurb: A hilltop Jyotirlinga above the Krishna river gorge at Srisailam, one of the few shrines counted among both the Jyotirlingas and the Shakti Peethas.

name: Mahakaleshwar Temple
blurb: Ujjain's Jyotirlinga, unusual for facing south, known for its pre-dawn Bhasma Aarti where the deity is ritually bathed in sacred ash.

name: Omkareshwar Temple
blurb: A Jyotirlinga on a Narmada river island shaped like the sacred Om symbol, reached by a footbridge from the mainland ghats.

name: Kedarnath Temple
blurb: A stone Shiva temple at 3,583m in the Garhwal Himalaya, reachable only on foot or by helicopter, open to pilgrims a few months each year.

nearestRail.name: Rishikesh Railway Station (railhead; Gaurikund/Sonprayag then trek)

name: Bhimashankar Temple
blurb: A Jyotirlinga tucked into a forested wildlife sanctuary in the Sahyadri hills, and the source of the Bhima river.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
blurb: Varanasi's Jyotirlinga on the Ganga's ghats, rebuilt in its present form in 1780 and now linked to the river by a broad new corridor.

nearestAirport.name: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi (VNS)

name: Trimbakeshwar Shiva Temple
blurb: A black-stone Jyotirlinga near Nashik where the Godavari river is believed to originate, its inner sanctum holding three small lingas for the Trimurti.

name: Baidyanath Temple
blurb: A Jyotirlinga at Deoghar also revered as one of the Shakti Peethas, drawing pilgrims who carry Ganga water on foot from Sultanganj.

name: Nageshwar Jyotirlinga
blurb: A Jyotirlinga near Dwarka marked by a giant Shiva statue, one of three shrines across India that claim the name Nageshwar.

name: Ramanathaswamy Temple
blurb: A Jyotirlinga and Char Dham site on an island linked to the Ramayana, famed for a pillared corridor among the longest of any Hindu temple.

name: Grishneshwar Temple
blurb: The last of the twelve Jyotirlingas, rebuilt in the 18th century barely a kilometre from the Ellora Caves.

name: Badrinath Temple
blurb: The Himalayan Char Dham dedicated to Vishnu, open only from spring to autumn before Garhwal's snows close the valley.

nearestRail.name: Rishikesh Railway Station (railhead; Badrinath is a motorable road-head)

name: Dwarkadhish Temple
blurb: Krishna's Char Dham temple in his legendary capital of Dwarka, its five-storey spire visible from far along the Gujarat coast.

name: Jagannath Temple, Puri
blurb: The Char Dham temple on Odisha's coast, famous for its annual Rath Yatra, when the deities are pulled through the streets on giant wooden chariots.
